reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Activity-defined DG population manipulated during acquisition; subsequent no-light context-specific behavior, physiological recruitment and contingency controls.

checks.reason: No explicit pre-execution consultation and transfer verification of original tagging, optical activation and behavioral Methods/supplements or validated protocols.

The tagging delivery/open-close/expression procedure and critical optical exposure settings remain unspecified without quantitative choices or concrete calibration-to-choice procedures. Proposed example timings do not resolve the targeting/delivery prerequisites.

Physiology, anatomy and blinded scoring validation are planned, but objective measurement-calibration acceptance criteria or a procedure deriving them, including scorer agreement/dynamic range and failure action, are not operationally specified.

Freezing fraction and test denominator are defined, but the movement threshold/minimum-bout rule and their calibration-to-choice procedure are missing. A promise to lock a scoring definition is not an executable quantitative endpoint rule.
Animal-level units, pilot variance and a meaningful effect are named, but no explicit precision/power target and calculation/simulation procedure connects these to adequate confirmatory replication.
The primary interaction/contrasts are identified, but the bounded-outcome model/interval method and multiplicity procedure remain future choices rather than an operational inferential specification.
Independent pilots and a subsequent lock are proposed, but the power/labeling/physiological parameter exploration lacks a complete bounded search and objective selection/stop rule.
No explicit failure-triggered revision specifies what remains fixed, refreezes the changed procedure and obtains fresh independent confirmation after troubleshooting.

Neutral tagging, verified window closure before aversive acquisition elsewhere, matched paired/unpaired and shock-only controls, first no-light T/U tests and separate physiological validation form a strong causal design. Assignment-based outcomes preserve nonresponders and missingness; coded raw records and event logs support audit. Operational calibration and statistical details still fall short of the strict checklist.
